author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A round of heavy rain is expected to move through Massachusetts on Sunday morning, prompting flood watches for parts of the state from late Saturday night into Sunday afternoon. Forecasters said the system could produce localized flash flooding and ponding on roads, especially where downpours repeatedly cross the same area.

The rain is expected to arrive from west to east overnight and become most widespread during the morning. Isolated thunderstorms are possible, although the threat of severe weather was described as low. Drivers should be prepared for reduced visibility, standing water and slower travel during the wettest periods.

Conditions are forecast to improve from west to east during the early to middle part of Sunday afternoon. Temperatures should remain in the lower 70s, held down by clouds and rain. The precise placement of the heaviest bands will determine which communities see the greatest flooding risk, so residents should monitor updated local alerts and avoid driving through water covering a roadway.
dek: Forecasters expect the heaviest rain Sunday morning, with localized flash flooding and roadway ponding possible before conditions improve.
headline: Flood watches posted as heavy Sunday rain approaches Massachusetts
